colours.Primary Function: Base Saturation Tone — Ideal for large areas of colour (e.g. shields, robes). High saturation colour, requires complementary green for cold shadows.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply in thin layers (layering) to build up saturation in heraldry and robes. Excellent base for glazing more intense reds.
colours.Role of Complementary: Cold shadow and natural contrast — green cools the red, ideal for recesses and shadow areas.
colours.Keywords: Shields, Capes, Layering, Glazing, Base Red

colours.Primary Function: Deep Warm Shadow — Used for very dark red shadows, or as a base colour to simulate wine, dried blood or velvet.
colours.Strategic Use: Ideal for wet blending on heavy fabrics like velvet or for simulating dried blood. Use in dark washes to create depth without resorting to black.
colours.Role of Complementary: Deep cold shadow — great for bases with dramatic lighting. Avoids "too warm" tones.
colours.Keywords: Shadows, Dried Blood, Velvet, Wet Blending, Wine, Recess Shading

colours.Primary Function: Base/Intermediate Tone — Warm and vibrant colour, excellent for highlights of earth tones or as a base for reddish and rusty wood.
colours.Strategic Use: Use in light drybrush for warm highlights on reddish wood or leather. Apply with stippling to create rust or earth texture.
colours.Role of Complementary: Cold complementary contrast. Ideal for metallic reflections and steel shine near warm tones.
colours.Keywords: Rust, Leather, Wood, Drybrush, Stippling, Warm Highlight

colours.Primary Function: Base Tone/Cold Saturation — The classic vivid blue. Used for fabrics (cloaks) and cavalry emblems. Requires complementary Orange for warm highlights.
colours.Strategic Use: Perfect for glazing on cloaks and emblems, building depth and smooth blends. Use in layers to obtain a vibrant and uniform blue.
colours.Role of Complementary: Highlight Contrast: Being a light and cold blue, a light orange creates the perfect contrast to simulate sun reflection on blue metallic surfaces or warning lights.
colours.Keywords: Blue Cloaks, Cavalry, Smooth Blending, Glazing, Emblems

colours.Primary Function: Base Tone/Blue Highlight — Lighter and less saturated blue than Ultramarine. Ideal for cold base layers or for highlighting edges of darker blues.
colours.Strategic Use: Essential for edge highlighting on bluish armour or fine fabrics. Can be mixed with skin tones to create realistic cold shadows.
colours.Role of Complementary: Warm light and subtle reflections — maintains balance between cold and warm tones.
colours.Keywords: Edge Highlighting, Blue Armour, Skin Shadows, Cold Light

colours.Primary Function: Cold Shadow Tone/Bluish Metal — Excellent for deep shadows of blue fabrics or as a base tone for aged and dark steel.
colours.Strategic Use: Base for non-metallic metal (NMM) in aged steel tones. Use in dark washes for deep shadows in blues without "dirtying" the colour.
colours.Role of Complementary: Strong contrast (warm analogue) — excellent for adding tones of dust, dirt or rust, creating an earthy realism.
colours.Keywords: NMM, Aged Steel, Deep Shadow, Deep Wash, Black Armour

colours.Primary Function: Neutral/Warm Base Tone — Used for cloaks and scrolls and as a base colour for mortar or light stone in dioramas.
colours.Strategic Use: Versatile base for scrolls, bones and cloaks. Excellent for receiving earth tone washes and for texturing light stone surfaces.
colours.Role of Complementary: Cold shadow for skin tones, leather or fabrics. Helps give depth without darkening too much.
colours.Keywords: Scrolls, Bones, Tabards, Light Stone, Mortar, Base Coating

colours.Primary Function: Highlight/Light Point — The lightest tone for Beige fabric highlights or for the most illuminated points of stone/bone.
colours.Strategic Use: Ideal for final highlights on scrolls, purity seals etc. Use for detailed freehand writing with a fine-tip brush over Beige bases. Perfect colour for illuminating the sharpest edges of bone surfaces or light fabrics.
colours.Role of Complementary: Soft cold shadows — balance warm light, ideal for light or bone surfaces.
colours.Keywords: Freehand, Purity Seals, Maximum Highlight, Teeth, Bone

colours.Primary Function: Maximum Highlight/Pure White — Used sparingly for metal shines, eyes, crosses on shields and the top of your OSL effect. Never use directly for large areas.
colours.Strategic Use: Use for precise light points on non-metallic surfaces (eyes, crosses). Crucial base for transparent colours and for secondary glow in OSL effects.
colours.Role of Complementary: Chromatic Cold Shadowing: As Offwhite is an almost white "eggshell" tone, using a diluted violet/blue in the shadows prevents the piece from looking dirty, giving an ethereal and clean appearance.
colours.Keywords: OSL, Eyes, Crosses, Specular Highlight, Light Point

colours.Primary Function: Maximum Light (OSL/LED) — The brightest point for lighting (peak light). Being fluorescent, it amplifies the light of your amber/yellow LED, giving an incandescent and ultra-realistic glow to the lantern bulb.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply over white base to maximise the OSL (Object Source Lighting) effect of lamps and flames. Use in thin layers (layering) to build up luminous intensity.
colours.Role of Complementary: Intensity Contrast: Essential for the light effect (OSL). Deep purple placed around the yellow source makes the glow appear to emit real light by pure chromatic contrast.
colours.Keywords: LED, Lantern, Glow Effect, OSL, Fluorescent

colours.Primary Function: Base Tone/Warm Highlight — Mainly for skin painting. Also useful as a warm, yellowish highlight for stone and earth textures, complementing your Beige.
colours.Strategic Use: Fundamental colour to illuminate the high volumes of the face (forehead, nose and cheekbones). Can be used to simulate the warm sun reflection hitting the staircase stones through soft drybrushing technique.
colours.Role of Complementary: Organic Shadowing: For skin, using a diluted dark blue in shadows (like under the chin or eye sockets) neutralises the orange skin tone, creating realistic depth.
colours.Keywords: Faces, Skin, Sunlight, Drybrush, Volumes

colours.Primary Function: Absolute Shadow / Occlusion: Used for separation between materials (e.g. line between belt and tunic) and for mixing with other colours to create deep shadow tones.
colours.Strategic Use: Essential for blacklining, defining contours and separating materials. Base for dark NMM and for occlusion shadows where light does not reach.
colours.Role of Complementary: Binary Contrast: Technically black has no complementary on the colour wheel, but its role is absolute contrast. White serves to define shapes through edge highlighting.
colours.Keywords: Blacklining, Black Armour, Occlusion, Absolute Shadow, Contours

colours.Primary Function: Neutral Transition Tone: Ideal for painting stone surfaces, metal weathering or for softening the transition between black and white without saturation.
colours.Strategic Use: Use in drybrush to simulate stone or concrete texture. Mix to soften transitions between black and white, avoiding too harsh contrasts.
colours.Role of Complementary: Weathering Contrast: On grey stones, shadows or stains of an earthy red simulate oxidation, accumulated dirt or exposed bricks under plaster.
colours.Keywords: Stone, Concrete, Neutral Transition, Drybrush, London

colours.Primary Function: Specular Highlight / Mixture: Unlike Offwhite, this is "Pure White". Used only at the exact point where light reflects (glow point) or to lighten highly saturated colours. Essential as a "spot primer" for transparent colours (Fluors/Gels). Without it, the fluorescent pigment has nowhere to "bounce" the light.
colours.Strategic Use: Reserved for the extreme specular highlight point. Use as a spot primer for fluorescent or transparent colours, enhancing their vividness.
colours.Role of Complementary: Volume Definition: Black serves to create technical delineation (Black Lining) around white, preventing the colour from "blowing out" and losing visual shape.
colours.Keywords: Pure White, Spot Primer, Specular Highlight, Mixtures, Shine

colours.Primary Function: Organic Depth Filter: Excellent for shadows on red fabrics or for giving "life" to skin areas (dark circles, lips or scars) as it is a rich and deep colour.
colours.Strategic Use: Excellent for creating rich and organic shadows on red fabrics. Use very diluted as a glaze to apply in skin recesses, giving a more realistic and "alive" look to faces and scars.
colours.Role of Complementary: Vibrancy Contrast: Mint green is the direct opposite. Using small points of green in the maximum highlights of a violet cloak makes the colour "pop" to the observer's eye.
colours.Keywords: Scars, Dark Circles, Alive Skin, Red Shadow, Organic Glazing

colours.Primary Function: Cold Light Contrast: Perfect for simulating moonlight reflections or cold light on metallic/leather surfaces. Acts as the "negative" of orange to balance light.
colours.Strategic Use: Use as a filter on metals to simulate moonlight reflections. Apply in fine highlights on leather to balance warm tones and give a touch of freshness.
colours.Role of Complementary: Cold Light Contrast / Reflection
colours.Keywords: Moonlight, Cold Reflection, Cold Metal, Thermal Contrast

colours.Primary Function: Energy Effect / OSL (Object Source Lighting): The light point for magic effects or bluish steel reflections under intense light. Due to fluorescence, it "vibrates" more than normal blue.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply over white base for magic energy or plasma effects. Thin layers (layering) build an intense glow, ideal for OSL on blue light sources.
colours.Keywords: Energy, Plasma, Magic, Blue OSL, Vibrant

colours.Primary Function: Sunlight Highlight: The ideal colour for making the "light point" on warm colours (red, skin, yellow). Gives a natural light appearance instead of artificial light.
colours.Strategic Use: Use in fine highlights to simulate direct intense sunlight on warm colours (reds, oranges). Mix for light skin tones.
colours.Role of Complementary: Complementary Shadow: Instead of using black to shade yellow (which would create an ugly sludge green), use purple to create deep, rich and natural shadows.
colours.Keywords: Sunlight, Warm Highlight, Final Highlight, Light Skin

colours.Primary Function: Realistic Dirt Filter: Its function is to unify textures (such as leather or earth) and create automatic shadows in 0.04mm grooves. It is the "doctor" of painting.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply in washes on leather or earth to unify textures and create automatic shadows in recesses. Works as a filter for ageing and dirt.
colours.Role of Complementary: Thermal Neutralisation: Umber is a very warm brown. If the dirt looks "too warm", a little blue neutralises the tone, turning it into a more realistic greyish brown.
colours.Keywords: Wash, Dirt, Unify, Leather, Earth, Recess Shading

colours.Primary Function: Cold Natural Base Tone — Ideal for vegetation, peasant-inspired cloaks and organic elements. Excellent for contrast with earthy tones and warm reds.
colours.Strategic Use: Use as a base for moss and small vegetation growing in brick cracks or between stone steps. Recommended to apply with the brush tip in quick, irregular taps (stippling) to create a natural plant texture.
colours.Role of Complementary: Cold shadow and natural contrast — green cools the red, ideal for recesses and shadow areas.
colours.Keywords: Moss, Vegetation, Stippling, Natural

colours.Primary Function: Deep Cold Shadow — Perfect for vegetation shadows, heavy fabrics and areas needing depth without resorting to black.
colours.Strategic Use: The perfect colour for the deepest recession shading in red cloaks and capes. Being the complementary colour of red, it creates a much more realistic and technically "correct" shadow than using just black paint.
colours.Role of Complementary: Deep cold shadow — great for bases with dramatic lighting. Avoids "too warm" tones.
colours.Keywords: Red Shadow, Capes, Cold Shadow, Forest, Depth

colours.Primary Function: Contrast Cold — Ideal for creating aged metallic reflections, light oxidation and complementary contrast in warm schemes.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply as a filter on metals to simulate verdigris (copper oxidation) or reflections on ancient armour. Adds a unique chromatic interest.
colours.Role of Complementary: Cold complementary contrast. Ideal for metallic reflections and steel shine near warm tones.
colours.Keywords: Verdigris, Oxidation, Copper, Cold Filter

colours.Primary Function: Warm Sunlight Highlight — Excellent for illuminating fabrics, leather and gold metals while maintaining chromatic richness without resorting to pure yellow.
colours.Strategic Use: Use in glazing on reds to intensify heat. Apply in fine highlights on gold or bronze to simulate reflection of flames or embers.
colours.Role of Complementary: Warm contrast — perfect for light and highlight in illuminated areas.
colours.Keywords: Embers, Flames, Gold Highlight, Heat, Warm Glazing

colours.Primary Function: Warm Earthy Shadow — Ideal for aged leather, rich rust and organic shadows on red fabrics.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply with stippling to simulate old rust, hard earth or very worn leather. Use in washes to create a "dirty" and heavy realism.
colours.Role of Complementary: Strong contrast (warm analogue) — excellent for adding tones of dust, dirt or rust, creating an earthy realism.
colours.Keywords: Hard Earth, Old Rust, Old Leather, Stippling, Dirt

colours.Primary Function: Chromatic Cold Shadow — Perfect for enriching shadows of skin, leather or light fabrics without "dirtying" with black.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply in glazing on shadows of skin, leather or light fabrics to enrich colour without "dirtying". Works as a filter for whites and greys.
colours.Role of Complementary: Cold shadow for skin tones, leather or fabrics. Helps give depth without darkening too much.
colours.Keywords: Clean Shadow, Skin Glazing, Filter for White, Chromatic

colours.Primary Function: Deep Luxury Shadow — Excellent for noble fabrics, dramatic areas and depth in high contrast compositions.
colours.Strategic Use: Ideal for wet blending on luxurious fabrics or for creating dramatic contrasts in fantasy figures. Excellent base for painting gems and crystals.
colours.Role of Complementary: Soft cold shadows — balance warm light, ideal for light or bone surfaces.
colours.Keywords: Gems, Crystals, Nobility, Wet Blending, Dramatic Shadow

colours.Primary Function: High Reflectivity Noble Metal — Pure high-shine silver for knightly armour, templar sword blades and silverware details.
colours.Strategic Use: Being from the Metal Color line, fluidity is incredible. Ideal for airbrush or brush in thin layers. Use for final highlights (edge highlighting) over darker metals to simulate the blade edge.
colours.Role of Complementary: Reflection Shadow: Deep blue simulates sky reflection or cold shadows on polished metal, essential for depth in TMM.
colours.Keywords: Silver, Armour, Sword, Metal Color, TMM, High Shine

colours.Primary Function: Imperial / Heraldic Gold — Rich gold tone for sword hilt details, ornamental crosses and buckles. Offers superior metallic coverage without lumps.
colours.Strategic Use: Excellent for fine detail painting with a brush. For shadows, mix slightly with an Umber Wash for an aged gold or keep pure for new and polished gold.
colours.Role of Complementary: Royalty Contrast: Deep purple in gold shadows creates a classic chromatic contrast that makes the golden shine appear much more intense.
colours.Keywords: Gold, Golden, Ornaments, Heraldry, Luxury, TMM

colours.Primary Function: The 'Liquid Talent' — Low surface tension black shade designed to flow directly into recesses for instant definition.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply generously over metals or cold colours to create technical depth. Essential for engine parts and armour where panel separation is critical.
colours.Role of Complementary: Maximum definition contrast.
colours.Keywords: Liquid Talent, Shade, Definition, Recess Shading, Wash

colours.Primary Function: The 'Liquid Talent' — Low surface tension black shade designed to flow directly into recesses for instant definition.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply generously over metals or cold colours to create technical depth. Essential for engine parts and armour where panel separation is critical.
colours.Role of Complementary: Maximum definition contrast.
colours.Keywords: Liquid Talent, Shade, Definition, Recess Shading, Wash

colours.Primary Function: Industrial Streaking Dirt — The definitive product for the 'Grimdark' style. Simulates years of pollution and rain accumulation on vertical surfaces.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply over the whole piece, let dry for 15 mins and remove excess with a cotton bud and Thinner. It leaves only the recesses dirty and creates ultra-realistic transition filters.
colours.Role of Complementary: Clean vs dirty surface contrast.
colours.Keywords: Grimdark, Enamel, Weathering, Industrial, Realism

colours.Primary Function: Base Metallic Paint (Steel) — The foundational colour for most silver-toned metals, such as weapons, armour, and mechanical components. Excellent coverage over black primers.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply as a solid basecoat for all metallic elements. Serves as the perfect foundation for shading with Nuln Oil and highlighting with Stormhost Silver.
colours.Keywords: Metallic, Steel, Weapons, Armour, TMM, Metallic Base

colours.Primary Function: Base Metallic Paint (Gold) — A rich, opaque gold colour, ideal for golden armours, ornaments, and elite details. Known for its superior coverage.
colours.Strategic Use: Use as a basecoat for all gold elements. Shade with Reikland Fleshshade for a warm, deep tone. Highlight with Liberator Gold or Stormhost Silver.
colours.Keywords: Metallic, Gold, Armour, TMM, Custodes, Stormcast

colours.Primary Function: Opaque Base Black — Foundational black colour for primers, basecoats, armour panels, and for correcting mistakes. Smooth and consistent finish.
colours.Strategic Use: Ideal for Black Legion armour or the under-suits of Space Marines. Use as a base for highlighting with greys like Eshin Grey and Dawnstone to create volume.
colours.Keywords: Black, Base, Armour, Black Legion, Corrector

colours.Primary Function: Vibrant Base Red — A deep, highly opaque red, perfect for armour (Blood Angels), robes, and lenses. Excellent coverage.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply as a basecoat for any red area. Shade with Agrax Earthshade for a dirty tone or Carroburg Crimson for a richer red. Highlight with Evil Sunz Scarlet.
colours.Keywords: Red, Blood Angels, Robes, Lenses, Base

colours.Primary Function: Iconic Base Blue — The standard blue for Ultramarines. A dark, rich primary blue, very versatile for power armour and uniforms.
colours.Strategic Use: Basecoat for Ultramarines' armour and other factions. Shade with Nuln Oil for a clean finish or Drakenhof Nightshade for more depth. Highlight with Calgar Blue.
colours.Keywords: Blue, Ultramarines, Power Armour, Base

colours.Primary Function: Flesh/Bone Base Tone — A versatile, warm off-white. Ideal for bone, parchment, pale skin, cloth, and light-coloured stone.
colours.Strategic Use: Use as a basecoat for any bone or parchment elements. Shade with Agrax Earthshade or Seraphim Sepia for an aged look. Highlight with Pallid Wych Flesh.
colours.Keywords: Bone, Parchment, Pale Skin, Stone, Base

colours.Primary Function: Midtone / Main Colour
colours.Strategic Use: Layering and gradients on cloth, sci-fi armour, or heraldry
colours.Role of Complementary: Dark Green (AK11146) — The ideal choice for Shadows OR Grass Green (AK11140) — The environmental contrast OR Mint Green (AK11143) — Only for cold light effects
colours.Keywords: Vibrant, Intense, Game Color, Acrylic, Drop Bottle

colours.Primary Function: Warm antique gold metallic — matte acrylic with high pigment density, suitable for brush application on miniatures.
colours.Strategic Use: Best over black primer for depth on 3D-printed miniatures; apply in thin layers for brush work; glaze with brown or umber washes for an aged appearance.
colours.Role of Complementary: Chromatic shadow — deep purple/violet provides rich contrast that enhances perceived warmth and shine of gold.
colours.Keywords: Vallejo, Model Color, Old Gold, Metallic, Brush, 3D Prints, Antique

colours.Primary Function: Bright, saturated metallic suitable for fantasy miniatures; provides a vivid polished gold finish.
colours.Strategic Use: Layer over a dark base for contrast; use for trimmed details and highlights; combine with bright highlights and brown washes for shaded depth.
colours.Role of Complementary: Creates strong chromatic contrast that makes polished highlights read as brighter and more reflective.
colours.Keywords: Vallejo, Game Color, Polished Gold, Metallic, Fantasy, Highlights

colours.Primary Function: High-quality metallic finish with aluminium pigments — thin and flowy, excellent for airbrushing and achieving smooth metallic surfaces.
colours.Strategic Use: Apply thinly (airbrush or multiple thin brush coats) over black primer for maximum depth; suited to smooth 3D prints and fine metalwork. Wait 12h before applying masks.
colours.Role of Complementary: Produces rich chromatic shadows and improves perceived metallic sheen in TMM approaches.
colours.Keywords: Vallejo, Metal Color, Gold, Airbrush, Thin, Metallic, 3D Prints, Aluminium Pigments
